solutions.latex: $f'(x)=-\dfrac{2}{x^2}e^{\frac{2}{x}}$. $f'(1)=-2e^2$, so it is differentiable at $x=1$ (not A). $f(0)$ is undefined because of $e^{2/0}$, so $f$ is not continuous at $x=0$ (B). $f'(x)=0$ has no solution, so no stationary point (not C). solutions.question: 11(e)
solutions.latex:
$\log_3(2x+1)(x)=1$

$x(2x+1)=3^1$

$2x^2+x-3=0$

$2x^2-2x+3x-3=0$

$2x(x-1)+3(x-1)=0$

$(2x+3)(x-1)=0$

$x=1$ or $x=-\dfrac32$ (no solution, since $x>0$).

$\therefore x=1$ is the only solution.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: progress towards a solution; 1: realises there is only one solution

solutions.question: 13(a)
solutions.latex:
Distance $=\left|\displaystyle\int_0^4\left(-\sin\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right)dt\right|\times 1.5$ (by symmetry)

$=\left|\left[\dfrac{4}{\pi}\cos\dfrac{\pi t}{4}\right]_0^4\right|\times 1.5=\left|\dfrac4\pi\cos\pi-\dfrac4\pi\cos 0\right|\times 1.5=\left|-\dfrac8\pi\right|\times 1.5$

$\therefore$ distance $=\dfrac{12}{\pi}$ m
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: progress; 1: correct answer

solutions.question: 13(b)
solutions.latex:
Tree diagram (1st, 2nd, 3rd draw): after a red draw the probabilities remain $\frac59$ red, $\frac49$ blue; after a blue draw there are 8 marbles ($\frac58$ red, $\frac38$ blue); after two blue draws 7 marbles ($\frac57$ red, $\frac27$ blue).

$RBB=\dfrac59\times\dfrac49\times\dfrac38=\dfrac{5}{54}$

$BRB=\dfrac49\times\dfrac58\times\dfrac38=\dfrac{5}{48}$

$BBR=\dfrac49\times\dfrac38\times\dfrac57=\dfrac{5}{42}$

$\therefore P(\text{1 red})=\dfrac{5}{54}+\dfrac{5}{48}+\dfrac{5}{42}=\dfrac{955}{3024}$

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1317_q14b_s1}

In $\triangle PBC$: $PC=h\tan 48^\circ$.

In $\triangle QBC$: $QC=h\tan 52^\circ$.

In $\triangle PCQ$: $PC^2+QC^2=PQ^2$, so $h^2\tan^2 48^\circ+h^2\tan^2 52^\circ=80^2$.

$h^2\left(\tan^2 48^\circ+\tan^2 52^\circ\right)=80^2$, so $h^2=\dfrac{80^2}{\tan^2 48^\circ+\tan^2 52^\circ}$, $h=\sqrt{2228.636719}$.

solutions.question: 14(c)
solutions.latex:
Cost per hour $=3v^2+15v+20000$. For $d=90$ km, $t=\dfrac{90}{v}$ hours.

$\therefore P=\dfrac{90}{v}\times C=\dfrac{90}{v}\left(3v^2+15v+20000\right)=270v+1350+\dfrac{1800000}{v}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct derivation

solutions.question: 14(c)
solutions.latex:
For minimum cost, $\dfrac{dP}{dv}=0$.

$\dfrac{dP}{dv}=270-\dfrac{1800000}{v^2}=0$, so $v^2=\dfrac{1800000}{270}=\dfrac{20000}{3}$, $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{20000}{3}}$ ($v>0$) $\approx 81.6$ km/h (1 d.p.).

$\dfrac{d^2P}{dv^2}=\dfrac{3600000}{v^3}$; when $v=81.6$, $\dfrac{d^2P}{dv^2}=\dfrac{3600000}{81.6^3}\approx 6.6>0$, so a minimum.

$\therefore v=81.6$ km/h is the speed that will minimise the cost.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct derivative; 1: correct value of v; 1: test showing minimum
